description: Longhorn beetles are wood-boring insects that attack trees and woody plants. Larvae bore into stems and trunks, weakening plants and causing structural damage, sometimes leading to death of the host.
symptoms: Holes and tunnels in stems, branches, or trunks
favorable_conditions: Presence of fallen or dead wood nearby
spread: Adult beetles flying to nearby trees
Movement of infested firewood, logs, or nursery stock
Natural dispersal by adults seeking new host plants
management: Monitor adult beetle populations with traps
Promote tree health to reduce susceptibility
Avoid transporting firewood or plant material from infested areas
chemical_control: Systemic insecticides (e.g., imidacloprid) applied to the soil or injected into trees
Contact insecticides (pyrethroids) on bark for adult control
Timing is critical: target young larvae and emerging adults
prevention: Quarantine and inspect imported wood and nursery plants
Remove dead or stressed trees promptly
Use tree wraps or protective barriers where feasible
source: USDA Forest Service Pest Fact Sheets
Scientific literature on Cerambycidae pest management
